Dr fimbria-mediated bacterial internalization in epithelial cells expressing DAF occurs through a mechanism that requires the AfaE- or AfaE-II fimbriae and that involves the interaction of the AfaE or AfaIII-E fimbriae with the DAF receptor, followed by the formation of a lipid raft and the recruitment of the actin cytoskeleton.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the internalization of Dr fibria-positive bacteria within epithelial cells expressing DAF, CEACAM1 or CEA occurs through a receptor-mediated, lipid raft-dependent mechanism that involves microtubules but not microfilaments.
the internalization of AFA/Dr fimbria-positive bacterial strains is mediated by DAF, CEACAM1 or 6, and CEA.
